description_full: FLEX LNG Ltd., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the seaborne transportation of liquefied natural gas (LNG) worldwide. As of December 31, 2025, its fleet consists of 13 LNG carriers in operation. The company was incorporated in 2006 and is based in Hamilton, Bermuda.

Each employee generates $15.6M of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $8K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 0× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity).
financial_summary: FLEX LNG Ltd. is a small-cap energy business with a $1.4B market cap on $348M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -0% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $141M in free cash flow — roughly 40 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.88× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 5.6× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.9× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 11.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 43% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 4.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
